claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\) be the real Banach plane
\[
N(s,t)=
\begin{cases}
\max\{|s|,|t|\},&st\ge0,\\
\sqrt{s^2+t^2},&st\le0.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\), write \(u\perp_D^\varepsilon v\) when
\[
N(u+\lambda v)\ge\sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2}\,N(u)
\qquad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).
\]
Then the least \(\varepsilon\) such that
\[
x\perp_B y\Longrightarrow y\perp_D^\varepsilon x
\qquad(x,y\in X)
\]
is
\[
\varepsilon_D(X)=\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_X\\x\perp_B y}}
\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}N(y+\lambda x)
=
\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]
Equality is attained by
\[
x=(1,1),\qquad y=(1,0),
\]
and by the norm symmetries. Thus this canonical mixed square--circle example has a sharp global modified-Dragomir symmetry constant even though the same example is used in the literature to show complete failure of global Chmieliński approximate symmetry.
integrity: The proof exhausts all unit-sphere strata, uses the complete norming-functional set at square corners, and computes every reverse line distance exactly through the two-dimensional quotient formula.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to the displayed real two-dimensional mixed square--circle norm and to the modified Dragomir approximation; it does not assign a finite global parameter for the distinct Chmielinski approximation.
title: Sharp Dragomir parameter on a canonical square--circle Banach plane
